items.title: Sidney Desvigne Interview, 1958-08-18
items.q: I remember when I first met Arnold Matoir, and he used to tell me about Tijuana and Juarez while we was playin' there.

ctx.x: What did? I know I'm a twi-a, and Louis Armstrong. So when they walk in, the fella said, he said, what do you say? Now you pull a little over my eyes, uh-uh, uh-uh, uh-uh. I don't know what I say. You remember he had to put a trombone down? And he take the horn up, and I know, this nigga out here fool with the music, you know? He was satisfied. Yeah, he was beatin' by it. He was satisfied. He was satisfied so long he saw us playin' the place, he started packin' up, you know? Well, he was satisfied he saw us…

And Arnold was a fine trumpet player. He played all right here. Juarez, Tijuana, he played all around Mexico, you know? Because I remember when I first met Arnold Matoir, and he used to tell me about Tijuana and Juarez while we was playin' there. But he used to do very nice trumpet. Oh, he was? Yeah. Yeah. Nice trumpet play.
I never got to know him or hear him or know anything about him, very little except what some people have told me.
